subject: data-rest
text:
- **Files (`~/.viola/`):** Plaintext by design (Established Decisions: Database / State Store). Protected by OS permissions only:
  - Unix: 0700 directories and 0600 files, except the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola`, which is 0700.
  - Windows: the inherited `%USERPROFILE%` DACL (user + SYSTEM + Administrators), or an explicit protected user + SYSTEM DACL for a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%`.
  - The protected owner-only DACL of a home viola makes outside `%USERPROFILE%` reads `D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)`, canonical SDDL spelling the runner's user (the local Administrator, RID 500) `LA` (as measured on `windows-2025` at viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity/report.md).
  - The strict-modes check runs at startup (Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control). On Windows a plain home made before viola (`create_dir_all`) is refused `Writable`, the refused entry an inherited allow ACE that grants a write right to a SID the check does not trust (read by the right, whichever SID holds it), so such a home is one the check refuses (as measured on `windows-2025` at viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds/report.md).
  - **Code-bearing artefacts:**
    - `viola run` always rewrites `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` files with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (`replace_private_shared`: a replace that fails counts as done only when the file already holds exactly the rendered bytes, which a concurrent start of the same version writes) rather than trusting an existing copy.
    - `instances/<name>/settings.json` (the per-session override whose statusline command Claude Code executes) is `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":"<pinned path> hook statusline"}}`. `viola run` rewrites it whole at every start, a revived start included, with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`, 0600), after the first snapshot and before the spawn, and never reuses an existing copy. Its command uses the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` path (§ Universal). It is written only on Unix, and only when every character of the pinned path is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :` (`viola_agent_claude::statusline::override_document`), since a shell runs the string unquoted; for any other path, and on Windows, no override is written. The child gets `--settings <instance dir>/settings.json` after `--plugin-dir <dir>` and before the caller's arguments, only when an override was written. The flag is the agent crate's constant (`statusline::SETTINGS_FLAG`), which `viola verify`'s Runs C and D read too (moved at chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). **Ratified:** a code-bearing file written at every start and handed to the CLI is a boundary widening the founder ratified (live, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the operator). The Windows half is cut by his word the same day and owed to the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements".
    - `<hash>` is a truncated SHA-256 of the exe bytes (the first 16 hex characters of the digest). Before reusing an existing `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)`, `viola run` re-hashes the file with SHA-256 and compares the truncated result with `<hash>`. On a mismatch it refuses to start (exit 1). The SHA-256 implementation is `sha2 =0.11.0` with `default-features = false` (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`): pure Rust, no `cc` on any of the three `[graph]` triples, passing the cargo-deny C-build ban; `tests/contract_content_hash.rs` pins it against published FIPS 180-2 vectors and the 16-hex truncation. A non-cryptographic fallback is banned (§ Data Protection). Because the hash is cryptographic, this catches substitution as well as accidental corruption. Tampering by the same OS user (who could also rewrite the folder name) stays outside the v1 boundary.
    - `viola run`'s start pins the bytes it has already checked (`viola_state::pin::pin_bytes`, under the key `pin::pin_key`: `<VERSION>-<16 hex>`); `pin_exe`, which `viola verify` calls, delegates to `pin_bytes`. An absent copy is placed, never replaced, a copy another start placed first is re-hashed before reuse, and one tree's release builds can key two folders (each in the groups below).
    - `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/{OpenConsole.exe,conpty.dll}` (Windows x64): Microsoft's ConPTY companions, embedded in the exe and written by `viola run` write-if-absent through `replace_private_shared`, never overwritten. At every start each is opened with `FILE_SHARE_READ` only and re-hashed in full (SHA-256, sha2) against the pin compiled into `src/conpty.rs`; the held handles deny every other writer from the check until `spawn_child` returns. Before the held open, `viola_state::strict::check_present` runs on `bin/<key>/conpty/` and on each companion that exists: a refusal is `PinError::StrictModes`, recorded as `strict-modes-failed`; nothing is written, loaded or launched from that folder, and the child runs on the inbox ConPTY. A mismatch is `PinError::HashMismatch`: the file is left as found, nothing is loaded or launched from that folder, and the child runs on the inbox ConPTY.
    - `ledger/stamps.json` is written only by `viola verify`, under its `.lock`, with 0600.
    - `marketplace/` is written only by `viola plugin install`: two manifests and `viola/.mcp.json`, whose `mcpServers.viola` `command` is the canonical exe that ran the install and whose `args` are `["--home", <the canonical home>, "mcp"]`, built by `serde_json`, no hooks in any document; each file rewritten whole at 0600 on every run (`replace_private`), each dir 0700, any other entry left as found. Claude Code runs that command for MCP in a session that installed the plugin. viola never reads the tree back nor re-hashes the command, spawns no `claude` and writes nothing under `~/.claude`: the user runs the two printed `claude plugin` commands.
  - **Probe captures:** `viola verify` writes its probe plugin and the hook-payload captures under `ledger/probes/<pid>/` (0700). The captures, `captures/<Event>.<k>.json` claimed exclusively by the hidden `hook --capture` arm, are transient, content-bearing 0600 files, and so are Run B's status line captures under `typed/statusline/` (0700; `StatusLine.<k>.json` and its `StatusLine.<k>.shell` verdict, claimed by the hidden statusline capture arm) beside the 0600 probe settings `typed/statusline.json` (Unix); the `questions/` (Run C) and `plan/` (Run D) roots each hold their own `plugin/`, `captures/` and an `answers/` dir of compiled `ProbeAnswer` ids; the `resume/` root (Run E) holds the same capture plugin as `typed/` and its own `captures/`, read by the `resume-session` check and `ledger::resume_variants`; a drop guard removes the whole probe dir when `verify` passes, fails or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (only this run's `<pid>` dir), and only a scrubbed `--record` copy leaves it; SIGKILL, a crash, a failed handler install and a Windows close, logoff or shutdown leave it to be removed by hand.
  - **Interactive probe dirs (outside the viola home):** Run A's fresh `viola-verify-*` dir under the OS temp root, and in the user's current folder Run B's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`, Run C's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/`, Run D's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/`, which holds a 0700 `plans/` (its `plansDirectory`), and Run E's `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/`. All are 0700 and removed when verify passes, fails, or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (a drop guard each; the repo's `.gitignore` carries `/.viola-verify-*/` for a leftover). The stop is Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` and Windows `CTRL_C_EVENT` / `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` (`cmd::verify::stop`, installed by `viola verify` alone; its handler only sets one flag every wait reads). A stopped run kills and reaps its child with no key, and its guards remove only what that run created, never by a pattern or a listing; it adds no owner record and no remover of an earlier run's or another process's dirs. SIGKILL, a crash, a failed handler install (ignored, fail-open) and a Windows close, logoff or shutdown keep the OS default and leave the dirs to be removed by hand: the founder's narrow entry (relayed by the overseer, 2026-10-10), and the event set the operator's P4 answer (chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). Run C's one `allow` runs `touch viola-probe-permission` inside its own dir; Run D's plan file lands inside its own dir, never under `~/.claude/plans` (as measured on 2.1.288 and 2.1.287: `~/.claude/plans/` 17 → 17 files across the re-run). These are the founder's live rulings on the dirs (2026-10-05 08:25Z) and on M7 = A and STOP 7 (2026-10-05), relayed by the overseer.

text:
- **Repository fixtures:** `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/` is recorded by `viola verify --record` from live sessions and committed, its `Mcp.` exchanges by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (below). Probe prompts must be synthetic. Before any write, verify scrubs every string and key (the home prefix, both separator spellings and case-folded on Windows, → `~`; the user word, whole word and case-insensitive, → `<user>`) and refuses the whole recording (exit 1, nothing written) when a drive path at string start, `/home/`, `/Users/`, `\Users\`, the user word or an email-shaped token survives. A screen fixture (`Screen.<phase>.json`) keeps only the rows that hold a compiled signature literal (the rest `""`), and a kept row the scrub would rewrite, or a username split across a row seam, refuses it too. The refusal names the fixture file and a closed check code, never the content: `unable: a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>`, or `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>` for a screen, with codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`. The founder ratified this named form live at this chunk's wrap (2026-10-05, through the overseer's AskUserQuestion, the closed code set and no-content rule shown). It was the fixed `a recorded payload still holds a path or a username`. Review recorded payloads for home paths, usernames and tool `input` before committing. A `workspace.repo` naming this repository's own remote is kept in a fixture: the status line variants' `workspace.repo.owner`, the remote owner's handle, is neither rewritten by the user-word scrub nor refused (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows `inputs#I3`, given after it was shown to him and relayed verbatim by the operator; its landing here is the overseer's application of it); nothing else in this rule widens.
 The `Mcp.<variant>.json` class (`Mcp.tools-list-1.json` in `2.1.302`) is a live CLI's MCP exchange: the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` `record` sits between one live CLI start and a direct spawn of `viola mcp` (no shell, no PATH lookup), reads each line through `take(MAX_FRAME)` and appends it to a 0600 capture in a private directory, never committed; its `fixture` step keeps the client frames up to and including the first `tools/list` request and each request's result keyed by method, applies the same scrub, and refuses through `ledger::screen_fault` with the file name and the same closed codes, never the content. The class is validated by `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json` and hygiene-walked like the rest.

subject: data-lifecycle
text:
_Key management and Data lifecycle subsections are omitted for Minimal tier. There are no keys at rest. `events.ndjson` retention and bounding is an open item owned by arch. Security's only requirement is that any rotation scheme keeps 0600/0700 permissions and keeps offsets valid (see the Decisions Log)._
**Accepted risk (verify's trusted runs, B, C, D and E):** Runs B, C and D are real interactive turns under a trusted parent. For each, the CLI persists its session, a synthetic-prompt transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` for the dead `.viola-verify-<pid>[-dialogs|-plan]` path, and the user's own global hooks run for that session, with the user's own status line in Runs C and D and in Run B on Windows (on Unix Run B's status line is the probe capture its one probe `--settings` names, the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows); Runs C and D add two transcripts per verify (the same accepted class, the founder's M7 = A ruling of 2026-10-05, relayed by the overseer, its option text naming the +2). Run B leaves three files per real-CLI verify: its session transcript, the `<id>-backup-<n>.jsonl` the CLI writes at its pasted `/compact`'s compaction, and the session its pasted `/clear` opens inside the same process (the same accepted class: the `/clear` session the founder's live answer of 2026-10-06T19:38Z, relayed by the overseer, its option text naming the one more transcript; the compaction backup the residual of the sixth paste, the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row (`inputs#I3`, relayed verbatim by the operator), whose option text named the transcript effect as unmeasured; as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row, `evidence/live-round.md` §Transcripts: the `viola-verify` transcript count 60 → 65, five per round — Run B three (the `/clear` session inferred, not read), Run C one, Run D one, Run E none).
 Run E, which resumes Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` from its own `-resume` dir with empty input, adds no transcript file although its SessionStart payload names a `-resume` project path (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, `evidence/live-round.md`: `~/.claude/projects/` transcripts 643 → 647 → 651 over two rounds, four per round: Run B two, Run C and Run D one each); it is the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows («Run E, шестой старт», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`). `plansDirectory` keeps Run D's plan file out of `~/.claude/plans`. viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude`. Run A leaves nothing. The print-mode probe leaves the CLI's empty project dir for its cwd `ledger/probes/<pid>/` under `~/.claude/projects/` (a `memory/` dir, no transcript), accepted into the same class by the founder's own word (live, 2026-10-19, relayed by the overseer), as measured on 2.1.296 and 2.1.302 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/evidence/switch-round.md`. As measured at chunk 2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes on the dev host: five such transcripts, `~/.claude/projects/` 13 → 18 dirs. The residual was shown at that chunk's plan review and accepted. The founder saw this class at his trust ruling, and the overseer's word was relayed by the operator at the chunk's wrap.
**Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI):** one `viola run` start of the CLI under a tmpfs `--home`, in a detached 80×24 pane, its cwd a fresh `.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root (a trusted parent), with no key typed; one `viola list` read against that home; at two instants, the pane's bottom three screen rows, scrubbed of the home and the user word, written to the chunk's `evidence/`, never a row above the footer; then the start is killed and its cwd removed. It left no transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`, since no prompt was typed (as measured on 2.1.302 at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/evidence/live-round.md`). It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer.
**Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`):** a live round that installs the plugin runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog (the dev-host prerequisite below). The rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key: on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, any other screen no key; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send. The CLI's writes are its own: its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), its `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings, `evidence/live-round.md`). viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`.
**Dev-host prerequisite (the real-CLI probe):** `viola verify` against the real `claude` runs from a folder the user trusts in Claude Code, whose external CLAUDE.md import is already answered. The CLI keys that answer on the git root, so an unanswered import shows its dialog in Run B's subfolder, and verify never answers it. On the dev host the overseer set the repo-root `projects` flags in `~/.claude.json` to the equivalent of "No, disable external imports" (`hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesApproved: false`, `hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesWarningShown: true`), as one atomic edit with a backup kept, on the founder's amended live ruling (2026-10-05 ~09:05Z). The flags were verified at 09:10Z and unchanged after every run. It also leaves the import unloaded in the founder's own subfolder sessions.
**Accepted risk (local availability):** until arch resolves `events.ndjson` retention, unbounded growth of the file can exhaust local disk. The impact is on availability only (the disk), with no confidentiality or integrity impact.

subject: bootstrap
text:
- **auth-scaffolding-baseline:** Narrowed to the local boundary; no auth library. Each arch amendment (Decisions Log) must be folded in before the first chunk that implements it:
  - Amendments 3 (`control-character` detail) and 6 (`MAX_FRAME`): before the `viola-core` chunk. Its `control-character` detail lands with the route's "Confirmed send" entry.
  - Amendment 2 (Unix endpoint move): folded into architecture §Occupied Resources (IPC endpoints) by the `viola-channel` chunk ("Wrapper channel").
  - Amendment 4 (`release-from-driver`): landed in the `viola` bin channel dispatch with chunk 2026-10-04-the-wheel (`viola_channel::ProtocolError::ReleaseFromDriver`, −32602).
  - Amendment 7 (largest-hook-payload ledger row): before the `viola verify` chunk.
  - Amendment 8 (SHA-256 `<hash>`): before the chunk that writes `bin/`.
  - `viola-channel`: per-OS listener hardening (Windows SDDL converted by windows-sys into interprocess `security_descriptor` + windows-sys SID lookup; Unix 0700 per-user socket directory + chmod 0600 after the bind + `peer_creds` euid check). The SDDL, the per-user directory and the 0600 socket landed with "Wrapper channel", ahead of Epoch 6's admission entry; the `peer_creds` decision and the directory verification stay with their route entries.
  - `viola-channel` client: the SQOS open (windows-sys `CreateFileW` + `Stream::try_from(OwnedHandle)`) and the peer pid (`Client::server_pid`, `TokioClient::server_pid`, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`); the verdict, pid + sysinfo start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at`, lives in `viola-state` liveness (`verify_server`, `ServerVerdict`), called by the root bin and `viola-mcp`, built on Linux and Windows; every client reads the snapshot only after the instance's strict-modes check (`viola_state::strict::check_instance`; the six CLI frame verbs and `link` / `unlink` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, the hook event and dialog paths through `trusted`, `viola mcp`'s frame tools directly; a refusal writes no line), then makes the liveness pre-check and the server check. The SQOS spike passed (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`); the client reuses the recipe `tests/channel_sqos_open.rs` pins.
  - `viola-state`: home 0700/0600 creation (the pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` is the only 0700 file) and the strict-modes check (`viola_state::strict`), including the trusted files; the read rule (Unix `mode & 0o077`; Windows no `READ_RIGHTS` grant to another SID) on the home, `instances/<name>/` and its `diagnostics/`; `check_home_tree` (the home tree at `run` and `revive` start and in `verify`); `check_diagnostics` (the diagnostics opens); `check_present` (the `conpty/` companions); and the `Readable` and `Symlink` refusals; on Windows, the protected user + SYSTEM DACL for a `--home` outside `%USERPROFILE%` and the owner + DACL check (windows-sys).
  - `viola-state`: SHA-256 re-hash of `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` before reuse. The hash crate is `sha2 =0.11.0` (Decisions Log `2026-09-25`).
  - `viola run` / `viola-state`: rewrite `plugin/<version>-<hash>/` files and `instances/<name>/settings.json` with the shared tempfile `persist` helper (0600, mode set on the temp file before the write) at every start, never reusing an existing copy. The `settings.json` override is rewritten on Unix when the pinned path passes the plain-character rule; it is not written on Windows or for a pinned path a shell could misread (§ Data Protection, Code-bearing artefacts). Every exec-form `command` they carry is the absolute pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola(.exe)` path, never a PATH lookup (§ Universal). `ledger/stamps.json` is written only by `viola verify`, under its `.lock`, with 0600.

subject: secrets
text:
- **Production:** No stored secrets in v1 (Cross-cutting Patterns: Config management, "There are no secrets in v1"; environment variables are not a configuration channel — the variables outside `VIOLA_*` plumbing are the test-only seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC`, compiled out of release builds, and the terminal colour facts `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, read in every build by `viola list`'s human mode only to decide whether and how deep SGR is written (they configure nothing, disable no control and widen no redaction; the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline; §Input Validation); §Security Anti-Patterns → Universal).
  - Inherited credentials (`CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET` and the other `CLAUDE*` identity variables) stay only in the `viola run` wrapper's environment. They are removed from the child by the R8 rule and are never serialised into events, snapshots, diagnostics or the ledger. R8 (operator ruling 2026-09-25, Decisions Log): every inherited `CLAUDE*` name (ASCII case-insensitive on Windows, exact on Unix) is removed except a name in the persistent set — Windows registry `Environment` value names, Unix `config.json` `claude_env_keep` — and the identity floor (`IDENTITY_FLOOR`, the 11 names measured on the Windows host, both messaging variables among them) is removed whatever the persistent set says. The strip, the registry reader and the logs handle names only and never read a value; `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` names the stripped (`env_stripped_known`) and kept (`env_kept`) names. A Linux dev-host reading stands beside the floor's Windows origin and differs (as measured at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/scratch-session.md`, names only): the environment `claude` 2.1.287 hands a hook, read in a child started with every inherited `CLAUDE*` name removed, holds 12 names, both messaging variables among them, four outside the eleven (`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`) and three of the eleven absent (`CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`). The floor stays the eleven: the four are not identity names (the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-07T11:37Z, relayed by the overseer), and the prefix rule already removes them whenever they are inherited outside the persistent set.

subject: errors
text: - `hook` never writes to stderr and never exits non-zero (Hook Contract). A security check failing in `hook` (server verification mismatch, oversized stdin, strict-modes failure) still ends in exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human. As landed, `viola hook <event>` runs the stdin cap, the `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` shape checks and the one-object parse and, on Linux and Windows, the server verification (macOS the recorded gap), and fails open with `hook-decision` detail `oversize-stdin` · `malformed-json` · `channel-unreachable` · `server-verify-failed`. Before it reads the diagnostics level or initialises obs, the event and dialog paths run the instance's strict-modes check (`canonical`, then `trusted`): a refused or absent instance, a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing directory included, exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append; the two `--capture` arms run ahead of that check. Its hidden `--capture <DIR>` arm runs the stdin cap, the absolute, existing `<DIR>` check and the exclusive `create_private_new` claim, and writes the capture raw; with `--answers <DIR>` it also runs the `take(64)` closed-`ProbeAnswer` read and `probe_body`'s payload shape check, and prints one `decision_body` body to stdout only for a mapped answer. Its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]` runs the same stdin cap and `<DIR>` check and claim, writes the payload raw and the closed shell verdict, and prints nothing on any path. On every failure it prints nothing, its stderr is always empty, and it exits 0 (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, capture arm; the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05 on `--answers`; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`), on the statusline form).

subject: errors
text: - `viola hook statusline` (without `--capture`) over a replayed snapshot (`read_snapshot_or_replay`) finds no `statusline_command`, so nothing runs and nothing prints; it exits 0 with empty stderr.

subject: errors
text: - A `viola mcp` frame tool (`send` · `wait` · `last` · `answer`) whose server check fails (the connected peer is not the recorded wrapper, or the check cannot be made) sends no frame and returns the result of an unreachable instance: `isError` `instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`; it adds no error word and writes no log line.

subject: errors
text: - A `viola mcp` frame tool runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance`) before its liveness pre-check; a refused check, like a snapshot that is replayed or absent (no live endpoint), sends no frame and returns the same unreachable result: `isError` `instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`, and no log line.

subject: errors
text: - The wrapper's `link` / `unlink` methods answer a failed `record` / `remove` as `-32603` with the fixed message `internal error` and `data: null`. At `viola link` / `viola unlink`, a wrapper error reply (a `-32602` included) is a wrapper fault, exit 20, and a `Refused` reply or an `ok` of a shape other than the verb's own (`link`: a string `since` and a boolean `already_linked`; `unlink`: an object) is an internal error, exit 1.

subject: errors
text: - CLI `send` · `wait` · `last` · `answer` · `pause` · `release`, as `link` / `unlink`, run the instance's strict-modes check (`client::refuse_untrusted`: `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`) before any frame: a refusal exits 21, prints the instance pair (`human::instance_state_pair`) through `human::refuse`, or under `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, opens nothing under the home and writes no line.

subject: errors
text: - `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start run the home tree's strict-modes check (`check_home_tree`, over the instance and the pinned copy's key) before the wrapper log opens: a refusal exits 1 with the home pair for a home-level refusal or the instance pair for an instance-level one, and opens no log, writes no line and starts no child (`revive --json` prints `strict-modes-failed`). `viola verify` runs the check on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log, and a refusal there, or `update_stamps`'s `StampsError::StrictModes`, exits 1 with the home pair, no step line, no summary and no line. On Unix a home under a regular file (unstattable) is such a refusal (the frame verbs: exit 21, the instance pair); on Windows that path stats `NotFound` and the `cli` catch-site line stands.

subject: errors
text: - `viola_state::stamps::StampsError` (`StrictModes` · `State`, the error `update_stamps` returns) and `viola_state::pin::PinError::StrictModes` carry fixed `Display` messages with no path or payload: `the capability stamps failed the strict-modes check`, a write failure its own fixed message, and `the pinned copy failed the strict-modes check`; `run` maps `PinError::StrictModes` to the `sideload_fallback` outcome `strict-modes-failed`.

subject: bans
text:
- NEVER write any channel frame (`send`, `answer`, `hook.dialog`, `wait`/`last`, `pause`/`release`, `link`/`unlink`, and `hook.event` notifications, which carry prompt and reply text) before verifying the server's pid (Windows: the connected stream's peer pid, interprocess `peer_creds().pid()`, which calls `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the SQOS-adopted client end) or euid + pid (Linux/FreeBSD `peer_creds()`; the client-side euid check owed to the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening") plus sysinfo start time against `snapshot.json` (on macOS, where `peer_creds()` gives no pid: euid + the verified 0700 socket directory only, per the recorded known gap; the euid check is never skipped), and NEVER take those reference values (`endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at`) from a `snapshot.json` that has not passed the strict-modes check in the same process.
 Every frame meets this ban in full: CLI `viola send` · `wait` · `last` · `answer` · `pause` · `release` and `viola link` / `viola unlink` take `endpoint`, `pid` and `started_at` from a `snapshot.json` read after `cmd::client::refuse_untrusted`'s `check_instance` passed in the same process, `viola hook`'s `hook.event` and `hook.dialog` frames after its instance check (`trusted`), and `viola mcp`'s tool frames after `check_instance`, each verifying the server on Linux and Windows (the CLI verbs through `cmd::client::connect`); only every client's euid check and macOS's pid and start-time check stay owed to "Unix endpoint and home hardening".

subject: bans
text:
- NEVER answer a `hook.dialog` with a non-`null` decision unless `ledger/stamps.json` holds a `viola verify` stamp for the child's CLI version. NEVER let any process other than `viola verify` write `ledger/stamps.json`. A stamp is what switches on dialog answering, including PermissionRequest `allow` (Threat Model Sec 1 config; architecture.md CLI Version Compatibility).
 The ledger has twenty-four rows (`LedgerRow::ALL`: the six spine rows, the four screen and timing rows, the four dialog-tier rows `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency`, the three framing rows `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear`, the newline row `paste-newline`, the three statusline rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits`, the resume row `resume-session`, the agents row `agents-join` and the compact row `local-command-compact`), and a stamp is read over the relied set (`LedgerRow::relied()`, counter `/24` on Unix; on Windows, where the status line is not wrapped, the first eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact`, counter `/21`), so a non-`null` decision flows only when every relied row passes: a home stamped `20 pass  4 fail` on Unix (`17 pass  4 fail` on Windows) records `cli_verified:false`, and so does a stamp holding exactly the fourteen older ids, or exactly the seventeen of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, all `pass`, and, on every OS, one holding exactly the eighteen of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows or exactly the twenty-one of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, or exactly the twenty-two of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, or exactly the twenty-three of a stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row; the hook prints nothing and `answer` exits 12 `unverified-cli`. The dated gap (R2, the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-04) under which decisions flowed on the ten-row stamp is closed.
